verdicts.summary: I couldn't break it. The combined rev-parse result is used only when the exit code is 0 or 1 and the stdout line count is exact. Every other outcome falls back to the same commands, labels and error handling as before. A wrong or missing index path is absorbed by orElseSucceed(false) and the index is rebuilt.
verdicts.scenario: Cases tried: (1) not a repo, exit 128: falls back to resolveGitCommonDir, which fails with the old label and no retry. (2) HEAD ref is corrupt or unreadable: either exit 1 with 3 lines, which is treated as no HEAD the same way hasHeadCommit's non-zero exit is, or exit 128, which falls back to hasHeadCommit. (3) A transient failure: the call uses allowNonZeroExit, so it never enters the retry at VcsProcess.ts:361. The fallback commands use the old operation labels, which never had retry. (4) Committed repo with .git/index deleted: stat fails and orElseSucceed(false) at :1021 rebuilds the index. (5) --path-format=absolute gives a canonical (symlink-resolved) path, while the old code could return a symlinked absolute path as-is. Both point to the same physical directory, so the temp index and its cleanup stay in the same place.
